items.headline: Midterm Election Day arrives with Congress at stake
items.summary: Voters head to the polls today as Republicans defend narrow majorities in the House and Senate. President Trump made a closing appeal before the vote, and analysts are watching voter groups that have turned against him during his second term.

items.headline: Haley Stevens endorses Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan Senate race
items.summary: Rep. Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary to Abdul El-Sayed, endorsed Republican Mike Rogers two days before the election. Trump invited her to join the GOP as Democrats condemned the move.

items.headline: Iran's delegation leaves talks in Qatar
items.summary: Iran's negotiators left talks in Qatar after a tense weekend. There is concern that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu could push for new strikes.

items.headline: Judge dismisses charges against ex-FBI agents in Hunter Biden case
items.summary: A judge dismissed charges against former FBI agents accused of lying about Hunter Biden, citing 'weaponization.' The Justice Department could still seek a new indictment from a grand jury.

items.headline: Nine killed as business jet crashes in South Florida
items.summary: A jet flying from Austin, Texas, to the Bahamas crashed into a South Florida neighborhood, killing all nine people aboard. Federal officials are investigating the crash.

items.headline: Sen. Chris Murphy hospitalized after a stroke
items.summary: Connecticut Sen. Chris Murphy was hospitalized after experiencing arm numbness at his son's hockey game. His office says he is responding well to treatment and is expected to fully recover.

items.headline: Fake emergency alerts hit Ukraine and Russia as limited ceasefire ends
items.summary: Ukraine and Russia both reported fake emergency alerts after cyberattacks targeted alert apps. The incidents came as a limited ceasefire ended, and no link between them was confirmed.

items.headline: FBI blames North Korea for $6.3 billion Binance heist
items.summary: The FBI said North Korea was behind the $6.3 billion theft from the Binance crypto exchange, the largest crypto hack on record. It linked the attack to the group behind an earlier hack of Bybit.

items.headline: Carney reports progress in U.S.-Canada trade talks
items.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said trade talks with the United States are making progress on an outline covering jobs, costs and Canadian sovereignty. President Trump spoke of the 'concept' of a deal.

items.headline: Snowstorms carry microplastics to remote Sierra Nevada
items.summary: Researchers found that snowstorms are depositing large numbers of tiny plastic particles in remote parts of California's Sierra Nevada. Snowmelt from the range supplies much of the region's fresh water.

digest.overview:
Americans vote today in midterms that will decide control of Congress; Democrats need a net gain of four Senate seats and three House seats, and more than 54 million ballots were cast early. President Trump closed his campaign at the Reflecting Pool, vowing to be "Mr. Veto" if Democrats win. Michigan Democrat Haley Stevens endorsed Republican Mike Rogers for Senate. A judge threw out a Justice Department suit to block certification of Alaska's Senate result, and the department will appeal. Another judge dismissed charges against ex-FBI agents accused of lying about Hunter Biden. Sen. Chris Murphy was hospitalized after a stroke. A jet crash in Palm Beach County killed nine. The FBI blamed North Korea for the $6.3 billion Binance heist, and Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum for about $115 billion.

Abroad, Iran's delegation left talks in Qatar, with the Strait of Hormuz still closed to shipping. A Russian strike near Zaporizhzhia killed at least 18 civilians, and Ukraine and Russia reported fake alerts after cyberattacks as a limited ceasefire ended. Israeli officials said election results will stand after Benjamin Netanyahu claimed Arabs stole the vote. South Korean President Lee Jae-myung presented a record 821 trillion won budget, and North Korea claimed its first cluster-warhead cruise missile test. Japan launched a national disaster agency. Iliana Yotova won Bulgaria's presidency, Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever resigned over a budget impasse, and cyberattacks spoiled food in supermarket freezers across Europe. Congo's Ebola toll reached 5,376.

home.overview:
Chicago routed Seattle 34–17 on Monday night to move to 6-2, a day after Denver beat Kansas City 28–24 to take first in the AFC West and Pittsburgh crushed Cleveland 27–6 to lead the AFC North. Lamar Jackson is headed to injured reserve with a thumb injury after Buffalo's 36–10 win over Baltimore, and Cincinnati outlasted Tennessee 43–36 in overtime. In the NBA, New Orleans handed Memphis its first loss, 135–134 in overtime, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 43 in Oklahoma City's win at Cleveland, and Luka Dončić posted 45 and 42 in back-to-back Lakers wins. The league sits out Election Day before a 14-game Wednesday. MLB free agency is open, with eight players handed $23.15 million qualifying offers.

Kai Havertz's goal gave Arsenal a 1–0 win at Anfield and a three-point Premier League lead, and Everton won 1–0 at Newcastle. Real Madrid won 3–0 at Racing to sit a point behind Atlético, who host leaders Barcelona on Sunday. The Champions League returns tonight with Aston Villa at Barcelona, PSG at Villarreal and Bayern at Atlético, and MLS closes its regular season on Decision Day Saturday. In the KBO, top seed KT Wiz and Samsung opened the Korean Series in Suwon on Tuesday.

brief: The best-of-seven Korean Series between regular-season champion KT Wiz and Samsung opened Tuesday at 6:30 p.m. KST at KT Wiz Park in Suwon.
Davis Daniel (5-2, 2.13 ERA) started Game 1 for KT against Samsung's Choi Won-tae, who has a 14.14 ERA in seven previous Korean Series games.
Games 1 and 2 are in Suwon, Games 3–5 in Daegu (Nov. 6–8, Game 5 if needed), and Games 6–7 back in Suwon on Nov. 10–11 if needed.
KT have not played since Oct. 12, while Samsung won the regular-season series against them 9–7.

brief: MLB free agency opened Monday, Nov. 2, and the qualifying offer acceptance deadline is Nov. 17.
Eight players received $23.15 million qualifying offers: Randy Arozarena, Jake Bauers, David Bednar, Ryan Jeffers, Brandon Lowe, Adrián Morejón, Trevor Rogers and Seiya Suzuki.
The champion Brewers exercised their 2027 option on World Series MVP William Contreras and declined options on Gary Sánchez and Antonio Senzatela.
The Rays picked up Drew Rasmussen's $20 million option, and Hanshin posted Central League triple crown winner Teruaki Sato to MLB clubs.
Gold Gloves went to Pete Crow-Armstrong for a second straight year, with the Red Sox and Diamondbacks leading all teams with three winners each.
The GM Meetings run Nov. 9–12 in Las Vegas, and the labor deal expires Dec. 1 with a lockout expected.

brief: Chicago routed defending champion Seattle 34–17 on Monday night to improve to 6-2, with newly acquired Jeffery Simmons posting a sack and Caleb Williams throwing for 247 yards and a touchdown.
Denver beat Kansas City 28–24 to seize first place in the AFC West after a false-start penalty wiped out an apparent Chiefs go-ahead touchdown.
Baltimore's Lamar Jackson is headed for injured reserve and thumb surgery after getting hurt against Buffalo in a 36–10 Bills win.
Arizona stunned Dallas 33–30 in overtime, and Cincinnati outlasted Tennessee 43–36 in overtime for a final score never before seen in NFL history.
Pittsburgh took the AFC North lead by beating Cleveland 27–6, Detroit edged Minnesota 19–15 but lost linebacker Jack Campbell to a serious injury, and Tampa Bay blanked Atlanta 16–0.
Week 9 opens Thursday with Jacksonville at Baltimore, and the NFL trade deadline is Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET.

brief: Kai Havertz scored from a Declan Rice cross as Arsenal won 1–0 at Liverpool, their first league win at Anfield in 14 years, to go three points clear of Manchester City at the top; Liverpool stay fifth, nine points back.
Everton won 1–0 at Newcastle, handing Matthias Jaissle a second straight home defeat as fans booed and the coach accused his players of ignoring the game plan.
Real Madrid won 3–0 at Racing Santander on Sunday with first-half goals from Kylian Mbappé (penalty), Jude Bellingham and Yan Diomande; Athletic Club beat Real Sociedad 2–1 in the Basque derby.
Elsewhere on Sunday, Frankfurt beat Hamburg 3–1 in the Bundesliga, Getafe beat Sevilla 3–1 in La Liga, and Paris FC beat Monaco 3–1 as Lyon and Marseille also won to chase Ligue 1 leaders PSG.

Champions League Matchday 4 runs Tuesday and Wednesday, with Man United hosting Roma under pressure on Michael Carrick, Barcelona facing Aston Villa, Bayern meeting Atlético and Inter visiting Feyenoord without Lautaro Martínez.
West Ham sacked Nuno Espírito Santo on Tuesday after a 3–1 home loss to West Brom left them eighth in the Championship, with Mark Noble, Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville in temporary charge.
